description: 2 tactical challenges for White in the Jerome Gambit. Sacrifice the bishop on f7 with 4.Bxf7+!? and hunt the black king.

drills.briefExplanation: 4.Bxf7+ Kxf7 5.Nxe5+ Nxe5?? 6.Qh5+ g6 7.Qxe5 — punish Black's greed and emerge a piece up.
drills.description: White to play. Black develops naturally with 3...Bc5 — sacrifice with the Jerome 4.Bxf7+!.
drills.explanation: The Jerome Gambit: White gives up the bishop for a raging initiative. After 4...Kxf7 5.Nxe5+ Black must NOT get greedy: 5...Nxe5?? 6.Qh5+ g6 7.Qxe5 wins the knight with a continuing attack — Black's king is drafty and White's pieces pour in. The whole gambit lives or dies on Black's 5th move.
drills.name: The Bishop Sacrifice

drills.briefExplanation: 5...Ke6! 6.Qg4+ Kf6 7.Qf5+ Ke7 — the king walks home through the center and the gambit fizzles.
drills.description: White to play. Black took the bishop and you're checking on e5 — but Black won't take the knight.
drills.explanation: This is why the Jerome is unsound at master level: 5...Ke6! calmly walks the king toward safety. After 6.Qg4+ Kf6 7.Qf5+ Ke8 is coming via e7 — White's checks run out, the king reaches home, and White is down a bishop for nothing. Knowing the refutation is as important as knowing the trap.
drills.name: The King Walk Refutation
